statement: The baseline used in this part. For the modern fundamental localizers fixed on the first page, $\Winfty\subseteq\W$, and $\W$ is strongly saturated and closed under retracts in $\Cat^{[1]}$. Neither assertion requires accessibility. Consequently a specified zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences of categories preserves $\W$-asphericity, and a commutative square whose vertical arrows are in $\Winfty$ transfers membership of its horizontal arrows in $\W$ in both directions.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Cisinski 2004 Theorem 2.2.11; XVI Loc (1 ter,3 bis)
notes: Modern relative-Theorem-A convention; no accessibility assumption.

statement: Forward gluing is automatic under relative Theorem A. Let $J$ be a small category, $F,G:J\to\Cat$ covariant functors, and $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ a natural transformation with $\eta_j\in\W$ for every $j$. The functor $\int_J\eta:\int_JF\to\int_JG$ belongs to $\W$. In particular every modern fundamental localizer satisfies Loc (6 a), and the augmentation from the Grothendieck construction of a sieve-cover span to its union is in $\Winfty$.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII W(7) forward; XVI Loc (6 a,6 B)
notes: Objectwise Grothendieck-construction comparison specified; empty diagrams included.

statement: A functorial categorical homotopy cofibre. For every functor $g:A\to B$ define $M_g$ on disjoint layers $A$ and $B$, with their original internal arrows and \[ \Hom_{M_g}(a,b)=\Hom_B(g(a),b),\qquad \Hom_{M_g}(b,a)=\varnothing. \] Composition of crossing arrows is induced by $g$ and composition in $B$. Adjoin an object $t$, with $\Hom(a,t)=\{*\}$ for every $a\in A$ and no arrows between $t$ and the $B$-layer. Call the resulting category $K(g)$. There is a functorial homotopy-pushout square of spaces \[ \begin{tikzcd} BA\arrow[r,"Bg"]\arrow[d]&BB\arrow[d]\\ *\arrow[r]&BK(g), \end{tikzcd} \] where $t$ supplies the basepoint. Thus $K(g)$ represents the unpointed homotopy cofibre, based at its cone point. A commutative square of functors induces a specified functor of these categories. If both vertical functors are in $\W$, the induced functor on $K(-)$ is in $\W$.
notes: Explicit functorial category K(g); A empty gives B coproduct e.

statement: The manuscript cylinder and the exact cofibration hypothesis. Let $\Cof_\W$ mean the functors $i:A\to B$ for which $B\amalg_A(-):A\backslash\Cat\to B\backslash\Cat$ preserves every $\W$-map. Every classical Dwyer map is in $\Cof_\W$. Every functor $g:A\to B$ has a functorial factorization $g=p_gj_g$, with $j_g$ a Dwyer map and $p_g\in\Winfty$. The ordinary pushout $e\amalg_A\operatorname{Cyl}(g)$ is a categorical homotopy cofibre of $g$.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms. 228–234; XVI Loc (6 A,6 A')
notes: The manuscript uses products with endpoints, not pushout-products. Thomason 5.3(3) is not used.

statement: The exact reversible-cofibre criterion: Lead 1. For a modern fundamental localizer $\W$, the following conditions are equivalent: Loc (6 b); its single-square reverse implication Loc ($6'$ b); the biconditional Loc (6 C) for every $\W$-homotopy-cocartesian square; and \begin{equation}\label{eq:cofibercriterion} g\in\W\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K(g)\longrightarrow e\in\W \qquad\text{for every small-category functor }g. \end{equation} Under these conditions Loc (6 a,b,c), W(7), and W(7 bis) all hold. Accessibility is unnecessary. The implication from left to right in \eqref{eq:cofibercriterion} holds for every fundamental localizer.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Lead 1; XII ms. 265–272; XVI Loc (6 b,6'b,6 C)
notes: Full cube and single-square versions proved equivalent; specified cone basepoints and retracts included.

statement: The two-cofibre argument: Lead 2. Every modern fundamental localizer satisfying Loc (6 b), or only Loc ($6'$ b), contains $\WZ$. The conclusion does not require adding Loc (6 a) as an independent axiom.
notes: No extra forward axiom; empty and arbitrarily disconnected sources treated.

statement: The finite acyclic category, with a complete certificate. There is a finite category $A$ with $35$ objects and $159$ arrows, all identities included, for which $BA$ is connected and integrally acyclic and $\pi_1(BA)\ne1$.
notes: 35 objects, 159 arrows; integral Smith forms and nontrivial A5 quotient checked.

statement: The reverse axiom for $\Winfty$, including Dwyer cobase changes. The assertions that $\Winfty$ satisfies W(7), W(7 bis), Loc (6 b), or Loc (6 c) are false. XII Theorem 2 at ms.~78 and XVI Theorem 5.4 insofar as it includes Loc (6) are false. The reverse edge implications can fail even for a pushout along a classical Dwyer map.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII Theorem 2 ms. 78; XVI Theorem 5.4 ms. 79
notes: 37-object two-cone counterexample and actual Dwyer-cylinder counterexample.

statement: The two variances of the one-point collage. For a covariant functor $H:A\to\mathbf{Set}$, let $A_H$ be obtained by adjoining $x$ with $\Hom(x,a)=H(a)$, no arrows $a\to x$, and $\End(x)=\{\id\}$. If $E=\El_A(H)$ and $\pi:E\to A$, there is a literal isomorphism of simplicial sets \[ NA_H\cong NA\amalg_{NE}(\Delta^0*NE). \] Thus $BA_H$ is the homotopy cofibre of $B\pi$. Dually, for $H:A^{\op}\to\mathbf{Set}$, adjoining a last object $t$ with $\Hom(a,t)=H(a)$ gives the right-cone formula with $NE*\Delta^0$. Under the equivalent axioms in \claimref{B.5}, a full sieve $U\subset X$ with one complementary object $t$ and $\End_X(t)=\{\id\}$ satisfies \[ U\to X\in\W\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad U/t\to e\in\W. \]
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms. 85; TOTASPH A.10–A.11, B.1–B.2, F.20
notes: Both variances; one-point complement has only identity endomorphism.

statement: An explicit nontrivial acyclic group. Every small group $H$ embeds in a small acyclic group $M(H)$ of cardinality at most $\max(|H|,\aleph_0)$; for infinite $H$ equality holds. In particular $M(\mathbb Z)$ is countable, nontrivial, and acyclic. Its one-object category has no nonidentity idempotents.
notes: Mitosis independently proved; the stronger simple-group claim is unnecessary and unused.

statement: The one-object test required after CATHOT. Let $G$ be any nontrivial integrally acyclic small group, and let $\mathsf BG$ denote its one-object category. For every fundamental localizer satisfying Loc (6 b), $\mathsf BG\to e$ belongs to $\W$, although it does not induce an isomorphism on fundamental groups. Thus such a localizer cannot require $\pi_1$-isomorphisms even on one-object sources.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: After CATHOT consequence for Part C
notes: All acyclic groups killed by every reversible localizer; nontrivial pi1 retained in source.

statement: The amalgam is a homological suspension model. Let $H\hookrightarrow G$ be an injective homomorphism of small groups with $G$ integrally acyclic. The double mapping cylinder of $BG\leftarrow BH\to BG$ is a classifying space for $D=G*_HG$. Collapsing its two vertex spaces gives a specified map $BD\to\Sigma BH$ inducing an integral homology isomorphism. In particular this holds when $H$ is acyclic, but it does not require that assumption, and it does not assert a weak homotopy equivalence.
notes: Specified graph-of-spaces quotient is a homology equivalence; H need not be acyclic.

statement: The upper interval is not the reversible class. The assertion that $\WZ\subseteq\W$ suffices for Loc (6 b) is false. In particular $\W_0$ contains $\WZ$ and fails the cofiber criterion.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part H wording; proposed upward-closed reading of Lead 3
notes: W0 contains WZ but fails reverse excision; four-object circle cofiber checked.

statement: Minimality of integral homology: the valid part of Lead 3. The class $\WZ$ of all functors inducing integral homology isomorphisms on nerves is a fundamental localizer satisfying Loc (6 a,b,c). It is the smallest modern fundamental localizer satisfying Loc (6 b), and is strictly larger than $\Winfty$.
notes: Integral homology gives the least reversible fundamental localizer; full cube proof by chain complexes.

statement: The incompatibility of the two poles, with the connectivity correction. There is no modern fundamental localizer satisfying Loc (5), Loc ($7\mathrm D_{\Winfty}$), and Loc (6 b). If Loc (5) is omitted, the unique fundamental localizer satisfying both Loc ($7\mathrm D_{\Winfty}$) and Loc (6 b) is $\Fl(\Cat)$.
notes: No solution with Loc (5); total class is unique only after omitting Loc (5).

statement: A nontotal reversible localizer kills no sphere. If a fundamental localizer satisfies Loc (6 b) and makes any sphere $S^n$, $n\geq0$, aspherical, it is the total class. In particular no nontotal reversible localizer contains $\W_1$.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: After TOTASPH sphere threshold; Parts C,H
notes: A nontotal reversible localizer kills no nonnegative-dimensional sphere.

statement: Both readings of the stability intersection: Lead 4. Let $\widetilde\W$ be the intersection of all modern fundamental localizers satisfying the stability list XVI Loc (1 ter, 2, 3 bis, 4, 6, 7, 8), with no prior inclusion in $\Winfty$ imposed. If Loc (6) includes its reverse half, then $\widetilde\W=\Fl(\Cat)$. If it means only Loc (6 a), then $\widetilde\W=\Winfty$. If the definition additionally insists, as the prose of XVI ms.~87 does, that $\widetilde\W\subseteq\Winfty$, there is no such localizer in the first reading.
notes: Unconstrained intersection versus an additional requested inclusion inside Winfty distinguished.

statement: What can and cannot retain simple homotopy information. No modern fundamental localizer on all small categories is a strict subclass of $\Winfty$. Even weakening relative Theorem A to the absolute version while retaining weak saturation and terminal asphericity does not produce such a subclass. A finer equivalence relation can instead be retained on finite CW or finite simplicial complexes by keeping elementary expansions, collapses, and the simple structures as geometric data. Such a structure is not a fundamental localizer. Merely localizing the category of all finite CW complexes and all cellular maps at simple homotopy equivalences does not retain the simple homotopy classification.
notes: Geometric simple structures survive; ordinary localization at simple maps loses the finer classification.

statement: The finite-poset observation survives without the conjecture. Let $P$ be the face poset of the boundary of a triangle, consisting of its three vertices and three edges, and let $\operatorname{sd}P$ be the poset of nonempty chains in $P$. The last-element map $\operatorname{sd}P\to P$ is in $\Winfty$ but has no inverse up to zigzags of natural transformations of functors. Thus strict categorical homotopy is finer than weak homotopy of nerves; this fact does not produce a fundamental localizer smaller than $\Winfty$.
notes: Finite posets P and sd(P); all monotone reverse maps have degree zero.

statement: The inclusions and the two poles. Every modern fundamental localizer contains $\Winfty$. Among those satisfying Loc (5), exactly $\Winfty$ satisfies Loc ($7D_{\Winfty}$). The localizers satisfying Loc (6 b) have least member $\WZ$, but do not form the whole upper interval above $\WZ$. There are strict inclusions \[ \Winfty\subsetneq\W_+\subsetneq\WZ\subsetneq\W_0. \] Neither $\W_+$ nor $\W_0$ satisfies Loc (6 b). For each finite $n\geq1$, $\W_n$ and $\WZ$ are incomparable. No nontotal localizer satisfying Loc (6 b) contains $\W_1$.
notes: Proper reversible class is not the entire interval above WZ.

statement: Total asphericity and ordinary final images. For a small category $A$, define $T_\W(A)$ by requiring that \[ B/(f_!1_A)\longrightarrow e\quad\text{belong to }\W \] for every small $B$ and every functor $f:A\to B$. Here $f_!$ is ordinary left Kan extension of presheaves along $f^{\op}$, and $B/H$ is the presheaf category of elements. Then $T_\W(A)$ holds if and only if every target $B$ of an ordinary final functor $A\to B$ is $\W$-aspherical. Final means that every $b\backslash A$ is nonempty and connected; no homotopical finality is implicit.
notes: Ordinary presheaf Kan extension; finality means nonempty connected commas.

statement: The entire interval is invisible to total asphericity. For every small category $A$, \[ T_{\Winfty}(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T_{\WZ}(A). \] Consequently these conditions are equivalent to $T_\W(A)$ for every $\Winfty\subseteq\W\subseteq\WZ$. Their intrinsic criterion is that $A$ be nonempty and connected and that, for every covariant functor $H:A\to\mathbf{Set}$, every connected component of $\El_A(H)$ be integrally acyclic. In this criterion ``integrally acyclic'' may equivalently be replaced by ``weakly contractible''.
notes: All covariant element categories and their coverings; empty case explicit.

statement: Above the one-type localizer, totality is plain asphericity. If $\W_1\subseteq\W$, then $T_\W(A)$ is equivalent to $A\to e\in\W$ for every small $A$, including the empty category. No accessibility hypothesis is required.
notes: No accessibility; final functors give pi0 bijection and pi1 surjections.

statement: The precise boundary for all sieves to be cofibrations. For a modern fundamental localizer $\W$, the following are equivalent: $\W_1\subseteq\W$; a category of homotopy type $S^2$ is $\W$-aspherical; every object-injective functor belongs to $\Cof_\W$; and every full sieve belongs to $\Cof_\W$.
notes: Every sieve is a cofibration iff W contains W1; four-object S2 category checked.

statement: The pushout-product substitution for the manuscript's cylinders. Let $n\geq2$ and let $\Phi_n=(0\to1\leftarrow2\to\cdots\leftarrow2n)$. If $S^2$ is not $\W$-aspherical, then the pushout-product of $\{0\}\hookrightarrow[1]$ and $\{0,2n\}\hookrightarrow\Phi_n$ does not belong to $\Cof_\W$. In particular this fails for $\Winfty$ and for every nontotal localizer satisfying Loc (6 b). Moreover the only class of full-sieve $\W$-cofibrations stable under taking this pushout-product is a class consisting of isomorphisms. Products with the endpoint inclusion, as used in \claimref{B.4}, have no such defect.
notes: Uniform n>=2 coend proof, complete n=2,3 computations, and arrow-retract obstruction.

statement: Stability of the unpointed derivator. Whenever the unpointed prederivator \[ \mathrm{HOT}_{\W}(I)=\Cat^{I^{\op}}[(\W^{I^{\op}})^{-1}] \] has the derivator structure under discussion, it is stable in Grothendieck's sense if and only if $\W=\Fl(\Cat)$. In particular none of the homology localizers for nonzero theories gives a stable unpointed derivator, although its equivalences admit the stable detection of Part F.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part H stable derivators; XVI ms. 119–121
notes: Unpointed HOT_W is stable only for the total class, whenever its derivator structure exists.

statement: The stronger separation from enough intrinsic fibrations. Every nontotal modern fundamental localizer satisfying Loc (6 b) satisfies Loc (5) and fails Loc (7 F). Equivalently, Loc (6 b) and Loc (7 F) together force the total localizer, without any accessibility assumption. In particular every nontotal reversible localizer lies between $\WZ$ and $\W_0$, with a strict upper inclusion.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Parts C,D,E,H; separation of reversible excision from Loc (7 F)
notes: Nontotal reversible implies Loc (5) and failure of (7 F); no accessibility hypothesis.
